Given $\rightarrow \mathrm{P}=1 \mathrm{~atm}\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}=400 \mathrm{~K} \\
& \text { Density }(\delta)=0.920 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \\
& \mathrm{R}=0.082 \mathrm{~L} \mathrm{~atm} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \\
& \mathrm{~V}=1 \mathrm{~L}
\end{aligned}$
The molar mass can be found using the density and the ideal gas law
$M=\frac{\delta R T}{P} \qquad ...\mathrm{(i)}$
Futting the value in equation (i)
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{M}=\frac{0.920 \times 0.082 \times 400}{1} \\
& \mathrm{M}=30.016 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}
\end{aligned}$
Let $x$ be the mole fraction of $\mathrm{N}_2$ and $(1-\mathrm{x})$ be the mole fraction of oxygen $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$
The molar masses of nitrogen and oxygen are
$\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{N}_2}=28 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}, \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}_2}=32 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$
mole fraction.
$(\mathrm{M})=\mathrm{x} \cdot \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{N}_2}+(1 \cdot-\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{O}_2}$
Substituting the values
$\begin{aligned}
& 30.016=x .28+(1-x) .32 \\
& 30.016=28 x+32-32 x \\
& 4 x=32-30.016 \\
& 4 x=1.984 \\
& x=1.984 / 4=0.496 \approx 0.456
\end{aligned}$
The mole fraction of nitrogen in mixture is approximately
$0.496 \approx 0.456$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of the wavelengths of radiation emitted when an electron in the hydrogen atom jumps from 4th orbit to 2 nd orbit and from 3 rd orbit to 2 nd orbit is
questions.solution:
Wavelength of radiation emitted from hydrogen atom is given by $\frac{1}{\lambda}=\mathrm{R}\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right]$
In first case $\frac{1}{\lambda_1}=\mathrm{R}\left[\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{4^2}\right]=\mathrm{R}\left[\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right]=\frac{3 \mathrm{R}}{16}$
In second case $\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{\lambda_2}=\mathrm{R}\left[\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\right]=\mathrm{R}\left[\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right]=\frac{5 \mathrm{R}}{36} \\ & \therefore \frac{\frac{1}{\lambda_1}}{\frac{1}{\Lambda_2}}=\frac{\frac{3 R}{16}}{\frac{5 R}{36}}=\frac{3 \mathrm{R}}{16} \times \frac{36}{5 \mathrm{R}}=\frac{27}{20} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}=\frac{20}{27} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If half of the space between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor is filled with a medium of dielectric constant 4 , the capacitance is $C_1$. If one third of the space between the plates of the capacitor is filled with the medium of dielectric constant 4 , the capacitance is $C_2$. If in both cases, the dielectric is placed parallel to the plate of the capacitor, then $C_1: C_2=$
questions.solution:
Capacitance of capacitor when dielectric of thickness t and dielectric constant $K$ is placed between plates $C=\frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d-t+\frac{t}{K}}$ In first case. $C_1=\frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d-d / 2+\frac{d}{8}}=\frac{8 \epsilon_0 A}{5 d}$
In second case $\begin{aligned} & C_2=\frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d-d / 3+\frac{d}{12}}=\frac{12 \epsilon_0 A}{9 d} \\ & \therefore \frac{C_1}{C_2}=\frac{8 \epsilon_0 A}{5 d} \times \frac{9 d}{12 \epsilon_0 A}=\frac{6}{5} \end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.q: Three particles $A, B$ and $C$ of masses $m, 2 m$ and $3 m$ are moving towards north, south and east respectively. If the velocities of the particles $A, B$ and $C$ are $6 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}, 12 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ and $8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ respectively, then the velocity of the centre of mass of the system of particles is
questions.solution: For the particles A, B and C $\mathrm{m}_1=\mathrm{m}, \mathrm{m}_2=2 \mathrm{~m}, \mathrm{~m}_3=3 \mathrm{~m}\begin{aligned} & \vec{v}_1=6 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}, \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_2=-12 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}_3=8 \hat{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \end{aligned}\therefore$ Velocity of centre of mass is $\begin{aligned} & \vec{v}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{m_1 \vec{v}_1+m_2 \vec{v}_2+m_3 \vec{v}_3}{m_1+m_2+m_3} \\ & =\frac{m(6 \hat{j})+2 m(-12 \hat{j})+3 m(8 \hat{i})}{m+2 m+3 m} \\ & =4 \hat{i}-3 \hat{j} \\ & \therefore \quad v_{c m}=\sqrt{(4)^2+(-3)^2}=5 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1} \end{aligned}$

questions.q: The potential difference $V$ across the filament of the bulb shown in the given Wheatstone bridge varies as $V=i(2 i+1)$, where ' $t$ ' is the current in ampere through the filament of the bulb. The emf of the battery $\left(V_{\mathrm{a}}\right)$ so that the bridge becomes balanced is
questions.solution: Condition for wheatstone: $\frac{R_1}{R_2}=\frac{R_4}{R_3}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{4}{B}=\frac{8}{12} \\ B & =\frac{4 \times 12}{8} \\ \therefore R_{B} & =6 \Omega \end{aligned}$ Using Ohm's Law: And, $\begin{aligned} & V=i_{R B} \\ & V=i(2 i+1) \\ & \therefore 6 i=i(2 i+1) \\ & \therefore 6 i=2 i+1 \\ & \therefore 2 i=5 \\ & \therefore i=2.5 A \end{aligned}$ Now, $4 \Omega \& 8 \Omega$ are in series $=12 \Omega\& 6 \Omega \& 12 \Omega$ are in series $=18 \Omega$ And both these are in parallel to each other $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \text { Req }=\frac{12 \times 18}{12+18}=\frac{216}{30}=7.2 \Omega \\ & \therefore \text { Emf }=\varepsilon=\operatorname{Reg}_{\text {eq }} \\ & = 7.2 \times 2.5 \\ & =18 \mathrm{~V}\end{aligned}$

questions.solution: Time to reach maximum height (A) from the top end of the window using $\begin{aligned} & v=u+g t \text { or, } 0=8+-10 \times t \\ & \therefore \quad t=0.8 s \end{aligned}$ Height from top end of window to A using $\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^2\mathrm{h}=0 \times \mathrm{t}+\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times(0.8)^2=3.2 \mathrm{~m}\therefore$ Total height $\mathrm{h}+1.8=3.2+1.8=5 \mathrm{~m}$ Time to reach the ground from height $\mathrm{A} 5=\mathrm{ut}^{\prime}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^{t^2}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 5=0+\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times\left(\mathrm{t}^{\prime}\right)^2 \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{t}^{\prime}=1 \end{aligned}$ Hence time to cross the window during its down and journey $=\mathrm{t}^{\prime}-\mathrm{t}=1-0.8=0.2 \mathrm{~s}$

questions.solution:

questions.solution:
Here vertical component of velocity $u=-100 \sin 30^{\circ}=-50 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ Let $t$ be the time taken to reach $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{h}=\mathrm{ut}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^2 \Rightarrow 375=-50 \mathrm{t}+\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \mathrm{t}^2 \\ & \text { or, } \mathrm{t}^2-10 \mathrm{t}-75=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}^2+5 \mathrm{t}-15 \mathrm{t}-75=0 \\ & \mathrm{t}(\mathrm{t}+5)-15(\mathrm{t}+5)=0 \\ & \therefore \quad \mathrm{t}=15 \mathrm{~s} \end{aligned}$
Therefore the horizontal distance between the cannon and the target $x=(v \cos \theta) t=100 \times \cos 30^{\circ} \times 15=100 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 15=750 \sqrt{3} \mathrm{~m}$

questions.q: The half lives of two radioactive materials $A$ and $B$ are respectively $T$ and $2 T$. If the ratio of the initial masses of the materials $A$ and $B$ is $8: 1$, then the time after which the ratio of the masses of the materials $A$ and $B$ becomes $4: 1$ is
questions.solution:
From the law of radioactive decay. $\mathrm{M}=\mathrm{M}_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{\mathrm{t}}{(\mathrm{~T} / 2)}}$
Here, $\mathrm{M}_0=$ initial mass $\mathrm{M}=$ mass left after time t $\mathrm{T} / 2=$ half live. $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \frac{\mathrm{M}_1}{\mathrm{M}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{o}}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{\mathrm{t}}{(\mathrm{~T} / 2)_1}}}{\mathrm{M}_{\mathrm{o}}^{\prime}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{\mathrm{t}}{(\mathrm{~T} / 2)_2}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{4}{1}=\frac{8}{1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{\mathrm{t}}{\mathrm{~T} \frac{\mathrm{t}}{2 T}}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}=\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{\frac{\mathrm{t}}{2 \mathrm{~T}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{t}}{2 \mathrm{~T}}=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{t}=2 \mathrm{~T} \end{aligned}$

\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A zener diode of zener voltage 30 V is connected in a circuit as shown in the figure. The maximum current through the zener diode is
questions.solution:
Current through Load Resistor $\left(I_L\right)$ Since the zener diode regulates the voltage at 30 V , the voltage across the load resistor ( $R_L=6 \mathrm{k} \Omega$ ) will also be 30 V .
The current through the load resistor, $I_L$, is: $I_L=\frac{V_Z}{R_L}=\frac{30 \mathrm{~V}}{6 \mathrm{k} \Omega}=5 \mathrm{~mA}$ Total Current in the Circuit ( $I_{\text {total }}$ ) The total current supplied by the source, $I_{\text {total, }}$, is given by: $I_{\text {total }}=\frac{V_{\text {in }}-V_Z}{R_{\text {total }}}$ where $R_{\text {total }}=5 k \Omega+2 k \Omega=7 k \Omega$. For maximum $I_{\text {total, }}$, we use the maximum input voltage $V_{\text {in }}=100 \mathrm{~V}$ : $I_{\text {total }}=\frac{100 \mathrm{~V}-30 \mathrm{~V}}{7 k \Omega}=\frac{70 \mathrm{~V}}{7 \mathrm{k} \Omega}=10 \mathrm{~mA}$ Maximum Zener Diode Current ( $I_{Z \max }$ ) The zener diode current $I_Z$ is the difference between the total current and the load current: $I_{Z \max }=I_{\text {total }}-I_L=10 m A-5 m A=5 m A$ Final Answer The maximum current through the zener diode is: $5 m A$

questions.q: A solid sphere at a temperature $\mathbf{T ~ K}$ is cut in to two hemispheres. The ratio of energies radiated by one hemisphere to the whole sphere per second is
questions.solution:
From Stefan's law
$\mathrm{E} \propto \mathrm{A}$
Initial area of hemisphere, $\mathrm{A}_1=4 \pi \mathrm{r}^2$
Final area of hemisphere, $A_2=2 \pi \mathrm{r}^2+\pi \mathrm{r}^2=3 \pi \mathrm{r}^2\therefore \frac{E_2}{E_1}=\frac{3 \pi r^2}{4 \pi r^2}=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.q: If $\mathrm{dQ}, \mathrm{dU}$ and dW are heat energy absorbed, change in internal energy and external work done respectively by a diamotic gas at constant pressure, then $\mathrm{dW}: \mathrm{dU}: \mathrm{dQ}$ is
questions.solution:
At constant pressure,
Change in internal energy, $\mathrm{dv}=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{v}} \mathrm{dT}\begin{aligned}
& \text { Heat, } \mathrm{d} \theta=\mathrm{n} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{dT} \\
& \text { Work, } \mathrm{dW}=\mathrm{PdV}=\mathrm{nRdT} \\
& \therefore \mathrm{dW}: \mathrm{dU}: \mathrm{d} \theta=\mathrm{nRdT}: \mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{v}} \mathrm{dT}: \mathrm{nC}_{\mathrm{p}} \mathrm{dT} \\

questions.q: A boy standing on a platform observes the frequency of a train horn as it passes by. The change in the frequency noticed as the train approaches and recedes him with a velocity of 108 kmph is (speed of sound in air $=330 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ )
questions.solution:
Using Doppler's effect formula:
1) Approaching Train:
$\begin{aligned}
& f_{\text {approach }}=f_0 \times \frac{v}{v-v_0} \\
& F_{\text {recede }}=f_0 \times \frac{v}{v+v_0} \\
\therefore \Delta f & =f_{\text {app }}-f_{r e c e d e} \\
& =f_0\left(\frac{v}{v-v_0}-\frac{v}{v+v_0}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0\left(\frac{\left(v+v_0\right)-\left(v-v_0\right)}{\left(v+v_0\right)\left(v-v_0\right)}\right) \\
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0\left(\frac{2 v_0}{v^2-v_s{ }^2}\right) \cdot v \\
v & =330 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
v_s & =108 \mathrm{~km} / \mathrm{hr}=\frac{108}{1} \times \frac{5}{18}=30 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s} \\
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0 .330 . \frac{2 \times 30}{330^2-30^2} \\
\Delta f & =f_0 \times 330 \times \frac{60}{108000}
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
\Rightarrow \Delta f & =f_0 \cdot \frac{19800}{108000}=f_0 \cdot \frac{11}{60} \\
\% \text { Change } & =\frac{\Delta f}{f_0} \times 100 \\
& =\frac{11}{60} \times 100=18.33 \%
\end{aligned}\therefore$ ANS: $(A) \%$ Change $=18.33 \%$

questions.q: A block of mass ' $m$ ' with an initial kinetic energy ' $E$ moves up an inclined plane of inclination ' $\theta$ '. If ' $\mu$ ' is the coefficient of friction between the plane and the body, the work done against friction before coming to rest is
questions.solution:
Let before coming to rest body slides up to distance s . $\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{s} \sin \theta$
From the work- energy theorem, $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{W}_{\hat{\varepsilon}}+\Delta \mathrm{W}_{\mathrm{mg}}=\Delta \mathrm{K} \\ & \Rightarrow-\mu \mathrm{mg}(\cos \theta) \mathrm{s}-\mathrm{mgs} \sin \theta=0-\mathrm{E} \\ & \Rightarrow \mu \mathrm{mgs} \cos \theta+\mathrm{mgs} \sin \theta=\mathrm{E} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~s}=\frac{\mathrm{E}}{\mathrm{mg}(\mu \cos \theta+\sin \theta)} \end{aligned}\therefore$ Work one by friction, $\Delta W_{\mathrm{f}}=-\mu \mathrm{mgs} \cos \theta=\frac{\mu \mathrm{E} \cos \theta}{\mu \cos \theta+\sin \theta}=\frac{\mu \mathrm{E} \cos \theta}{\sin \theta+\mu \cos \theta}$
